title: Macbeth
author: William Shakespeare
about:
Returning from battle, Macbeth and Banquo meet three women on the heath. They greet Macbeth as Thane of Glamis, a title he already holds, then as Thane of Cawdor and as a future king. Before the day is out, Ross brings word that Duncan has given him Cawdor. Macbeth writes to his wife. When Duncan comes to stay in their castle, the couple face a decision the witches never asked them to make.

Banquo has heard a promise too: kings will descend from him. Once Macbeth has the crown, that promise begins to sound like a threat. The couple who planned Duncan’s murder together soon start keeping secrets from each other. Listen for the sounds they can hear when no one else is listening.

angleCards.title: What do the witches actually say?
angleCards.text: One greeting names a title Macbeth already has. The next names an honor Duncan has just awarded him. Listen for the first person to mention murder.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to keep track of what the witches predict and what Macbeth decides for himself.

angleCards.title: Seeing a dagger
angleCards.text: Before Duncan’s murder, Macbeth reaches for a dagger that he can see but cannot touch. Later his guests watch him speak to a chair. How much can the people around him see?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow the gap between what Macbeth sees and what the other people onstage see.

angleCards.title: Lady Macbeth’s hands
angleCards.text: Lady Macbeth takes the daggers back herself when her husband refuses. Hear how differently she talks about washing her hands later, in her sleep.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow Lady Macbeth from reading the letter to speaking in her sleep.

angleCards.title: Who gets to be called a man?
angleCards.text: Lady Macbeth asks her husband to prove his manhood by killing. Macbeth puts a similar challenge to two hired men. Macduff has an answer of his own.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to compare what Macbeth, Lady Macbeth and Macduff think a man must be able to do.

cast.name: Macbeth
cast.role: Scottish commander and Thane of Glamis
cast.description: Praised for his courage against the rebels, he hears the witches name him king. In his private speeches he can imagine both the rewards of murder and its consequences in startling detail.

cast.name: Lady Macbeth
cast.description: She reads his letter and plans how to receive Duncan as a guest while preparing to kill him. Later Macbeth arranges Banquo’s murder without telling her what he means to do.

cast.name: The Three Witches
cast.description: They first meet Macbeth and Banquo on the heath. Later they call up apparitions for Macbeth. Listen closely to the wording of each promise and to what Macbeth takes it to mean.

cast.name: Banquo
cast.description: He hears that kings will descend from him. When part of the prophecy about Macbeth comes true, Banquo warns that a small truth may be bait for a larger betrayal.

cast.name: Duncan
cast.description: A betrayed king, he gives the former Thane of Cawdor’s title to Macbeth. He comes to Inverness sure of his welcome and grateful to his hosts.

cast.name: Macduff
cast.description: He discovers Duncan’s body and later goes to England to join Malcolm. He learns there what has happened to the family he left in Scotland.

acclaim.quote: the movement throughout is the most rapid of all Shakspeare’s plays
acclaim.context: Samuel Taylor Coleridge, “Notes on Macbeth,” Literary Remains, vol. II (1836). He is comparing the openings of Macbeth and Hamlet.

whyItMatters.title: What goes missing when someone stops speaking
whyItMatters.body: After the murder Macbeth cannot say “Amen.” At the feast he addresses someone his guests cannot see. Lady Macbeth manages both crises by telling other people what to do or what to believe. Watch for the moment when Macbeth starts giving orders without confiding in her.

whyItMatters.title: The noise at the gate
whyItMatters.body: Knocking breaks into Macbeth’s horror at the sight of his hands. In the next scene the drunken porter turns the same knocking into a joke about answering the gate of hell. Macduff comes through that gate and finds Duncan’s body. One ordinary sound connects all three moments.

whyItMatters.title: A promise heard twice
whyItMatters.body: The apparitions tell Macbeth that no one born of a woman can hurt him and that he is safe until a wood advances. Both statements sound like guarantees. Hear them again after the battle begins and ask where their literal meaning parts company with the safety he heard in them.
